questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.learningObjective: Choose the correct definite article

stimulus.body: Ausgangslage: «der.» The brief says 'der Tisch' for the table. In einer Arbeitsnotiz zu diesem Punkt heißt es: « der Tisch » Vier Aussagen werden angeboten; nur eine wird durch den Text tatsächlich gestützt.

questions.stem: Der Auszug wird an «Masculine nominative uses der.» geprüt. Welche Antwort bleibt bestehen?
questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: tisch is masculine, so the nominative definite article is der. On that basis "der" is the supported choice. Option A ("die") fails because it uses feminine form; Option B ("das") fails because it uses neuter form; Option D ("den") fails because it uses accusative form.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.learningObjective: Recognize Konjunktiv I in reported speech

stimulus.body: In einer Arbeitsnotiz zu diesem Punkt heißt es: «sei.» « Der Architekt sage, dass der Plan fertig sei » Vier Aussagen werden angeboten; nur eine wird durch den Text tatsächlich gestützt.

questions.stem: Wendet man «Recognize Konjunktiv I in reported speech / Konjunktiv I of sein is sei. / Konjunktiv I» auf den Text an, welche Option ist begründet?
questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: sei is the Konjunktiv I form of sein. On that basis "sei" is the supported choice. Option B ("ist") fails because it confuses indicative with subjunctive; Option C ("wäre") fails because it confuses Konjunktiv II with I; Option D ("war") fails because it confuses past indicative with subjunctive.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.learningObjective: Identify the dative object in a sentence

stimulus.body: Ausgangslage: «Bauherrn.» The brief states 'Der Architekt gibt dem Bauherrn den Plan.' In einer Arbeitsnotiz zu diesem Punkt heißt es: « Der Architekt gibt dem Bauherrn den Plan » Vier Aussagen werden angeboten; nur eine wird durch den Text tatsächlich gestützt.

questions.stem: Der Hinweis dieses Items lautet «The recipient takes dative.». Welche Antwort folgt daraus?

options.misconception: reverses the direction of the reasoning the passage sets out

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: dem Bauherrn is the dative recipient; den Plan is the accusative object. On that basis "Bauherrn" is the supported choice. Option A ("Plan") fails because it picks the accusative object; Option B ("Architekt") fails because it picks the subject; Option D ("gibt") fails because it reverses the direction of the reasoning that settles dative case.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.learningObjective: Determine case after a two-way preposition with motion

stimulus.body: In einer Arbeitsnotiz zu diesem Punkt heißt es: «Accusative, because there is motion.» « Der Architekt geht in das Büro » Vier Aussagen werden angeboten; nur eine wird durch den Text tatsächlich gestützt.

questions.stem: Wendet man «Motion selects accusative.» auf den Text an, welche Option ist begründet?

options.text: Dative, because in is always dative.
options.misconception: selects "Dative, because in is always dative" where the rule in the passage requires a different condition

options.text: Nominative, because it is the subject.
Genitive, because of the definite article.

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: two-way prepositions take accusative with motion and dative with location. On that basis "Accusative, because there is motion" is the supported choice. Option A ("Dative, because in is always dative") fails because it selects "Dative, because in is always dative" where two-way prepositions requires a different condition; Option B ("Nominative, because it is the subject") fails because it misidentifies subject role; Option C ("Genitive, because of the definite article") fails because it confuses genitive article.
